title: Task Scheduler
statement: You get a list of tasks, each a letter, and a cooldown n. One task runs per time unit, or the CPU may idle. Two runs of the same letter must have at least n other time units between them. Return the fewest time units needed to finish every task, idle units included.

example.caption: Tasks A A A B B B with n = 2. A B idle A B idle A B takes 8 time units. The two idle slots are forced by the cooldown.

idea.sentence: Each time unit, run the ready task with the most copies left, then park it in a cooldown queue until it is allowed again.

jargon.plain: A container where the biggest item is always on top. Here biggest means the most copies left to run.
A waiting line of tasks that just ran. The first one in is the first one allowed back, because every task rests the same n units.
A time unit where nothing runs because every remaining task is still resting.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the task letters and the cooldown n, e.g. ["A","A","A","B","B","B"], 2

presets.label: A A A B B B, n = 2

compare.bruteLabel: Scan all letters for the busiest, every time unit
compare.unit: comparisons (rough; the heap's log is at most about 5)

rows.name: Scan for the busiest each unit
rows.note: T is the total time units. Each unit looks at every letter.

rows.name: Max-heap + cooldown queue
rows.note: Each unit is one pop, and sometimes a push. With at most 26 letters this is close to linear.

rows.name: Counting formula
rows.note: (maxCount - 1) * (n + 1) + how many letters tie for maxCount, or the task count if that is larger. Fast, but it hides the schedule. Not shown here.

fast.takeaway: Always run the busiest ready task, because it is the one that will force idle time if left for last. Resting tasks wait in a queue until they may run again.

stages.title: Count and heapify
stages.note: Count how many times each letter appears and put the counts in a max-heap.

stages.title: Wake rested tasks
stages.note: At the start of each time unit, move every task whose rest is over from the queue back into the heap.

stages.title: Run or idle
stages.note: Pop the task with the most copies left and run it. If the heap is empty, this time unit is idle.

stages.title: Cool down
stages.note: If the task still has copies left, put it in the queue with the first time it may run again: now + n + 1.

stages.title: Finish
stages.note: When both the heap and the queue are empty, the clock shows the answer.

edges.title: No cooldown
edges.why: With n = 0 a task is back in the very next unit. The answer is just the number of tasks.

edges.title: One task only
edges.why: A idle idle A idle idle A. Idle units are counted, even though nothing else can fill them.

edges.title: Plenty of other tasks
edges.input: [A, A, B, C, D, E], n = 1
edges.why: There is always something else to run during the cooldown, so no idle units. The answer is the task count.

edges.title: Ties for the most
edges.input: [A, A, A, B, B, B], n = 2
edges.why: A and B tie for most copies. Both finish in the last round, so one slot fewer is idle than with a single leader.

gotchas.text: A task run at time T may run again at T + n + 1, not T + n. There are n other time units between the two runs. Off-by-one here is the classic bug.
When the heap is empty but tasks are still resting, you must still advance the clock. Do not break out of the loop. Check both the heap and the queue.
Array.shift() is O(length). The cooling queue holds at most 26 entries, so it is fine here. For a big queue, keep a head index instead. There is no built-in heap, so the shown file has a small one.

Ranging over a map gives a random order, so the heap is built in a different order each run. The answer does not change, because equal counts can run in either order. Tests must not depend on the schedule itself.
container/heap wants Len, Less, Swap, Push and Pop. Pop returns any, so write heap.Pop(ready).(*slot). Slicing the queue with cooling = cooling[1:] is fine for a short queue.

recap.key: Each time unit run the ready task with most copies left. Park it in a queue for n units, then return it to the heap.
recap.complexity: Time O(T log m), T = time units, m <= 26. Space O(m).
moves: Count letters, push counts into a max-heap
Each unit: wake tasks whose rest is over
Pop the busiest and run it, or idle if none
Park it until time + n + 1 if copies remain
